summary: Discovery call to assess Lark Holdings' security and compliance needs across Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment options. Focus areas: SOC2/ISO maturity, SSO/SAML SSO and RBAC, audit logs and retention, encryption and KMS/HSM integration, and data retention/PII handling. Customer leans toward Dedicated or Private for regulatory reasons but wants Hosted benchmarked for cost/latency. Agreed next steps: share compliance artifacts, schedule deep-dive on networking/KMS, and deliver Dedicated sizing/price ballpark.
topics: Audit logs, retention and access controls
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-12-09 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Torres (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (CTO, Lark), Elena Gomez (Head of Security), Raj Patel (Infra)
Shared docs: Redwood compliance deck (link shared in chat), SOC2 summary PDF, preliminary Dedicated sizing spreadsheet link noted

[00:00] Jamie Torres: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jamie from Redwood, with Priya on the call — how are you all?
[00:06] Marcus Lee: Good, thanks. Busy week but excited to get through this. Elena and Raj are on — want to make sure we cover compliance stuff up front.
[00:12] Elena Gomez: Hi all. We run regulated customer data, some PII, so goal is understanding where data lives, how it's encrypted, and who can see logs.
[00:18] Priya Nair: Great, we'll focus on those pieces. Quick agenda: SOC2/ISO posture, SSO/SAML and RBAC, audit logs and retention, encryption/KMS and private deployment options, then open Qs.

[02:01] Marcus Lee: To start, tell us the difference in security surface between Hosted and Dedicated. If we go Hosted, are we okay with their multitenant controls?
[02:15] Jamie Torres: Short answer: Hosted is multitenant but we have tenant isolation at the API layer, encryption at rest, and SOC2 Type II for the platform. Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and stronger isolation — separate GPU pools, option for dedicated VPC peering depending on plan. Private is fully customer-managed networking and control plane.
[02:42] Elena Gomez: Do you have SOC2 reports we can review, and ISO certs? Our procurement requires SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 for any vendor with production PII access.
[02:50] Jamie Torres: Yes, we have SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 summary docs — I'll send the redacted report and a short exec summary after the call. For Hosted we also offer data processing addendums.

[04:15] Raj Patel: On Dedicated vs Private — what's the practical difference for KMS/HSM? We need HSM-backed keys for some datasets.
[04:25] Priya Nair: For Dedicated, we support customer-managed KMS integration — you can bring your key (BYOK) via cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and configure key wrapping for model artifacts and persistent storage. For Private on-prem or VPC, we can integrate with your HSMs via supported connectors, though that path has more networking setup.
[04:47] Elena Gomez: Does Redwood hold unencrypted copies of data for inference? We need to know ephemeral versus persistent storage practices.
[04:55] Jamie Torres: Good question. For Hosted, we encrypt in transit and at rest. We keep short-lived caches (KV cache) for performance that are encrypted and configured per customer TTL; by default those caches are ephemeral and can be disabled. Persistent logs and traces are retained according to the plan; we can map retention to your policy.

[07:30] Marcus Lee: What about SSO, SAML, RBAC? We need SCIM provisioning and role-based access controls integrated with our Okta.
[07:37] Priya Nair: We support SSO via SAML and OIDC, integrations with Okta, Azure AD, Ping. SCIM provisioning is available for user sync in Dedicated and Private customers; Hosted also supports SSO and manual provisioning. RBAC is role-based at the token and UI level, can restrict access to models, billing, and audit logs.
[08:02] Elena Gomez: Will audit logs be tamper-evident? We need immutable trails for security reviews.
[08:10] Jamie Torres: Audit logs are write-once in our logging pipeline and can be forwarded to your SIEM (Splunk/Chronicle) via syslog or cloud sink. For Dedicated/Private we can provide direct log routing into your audit stack so you own the logs.

[09:45] Raj Patel: Network requirements — if we do Private, how much networking work is it? Does Redwood manage the control plane or is it entirely customer-managed?
[09:55] Priya Nair: Private offers a customer-managed control plane with an option for Redwood to assist in setup. For VPC deployments we require specific port ranges for the runtime, peering or private link setup, and a nat/bastion for updates. We have a detailed network checklist; I'll share it.

[12:20] Marcus Lee: Latency and fallback — if we host in our VPC, we still want fallback to a hosted endpoint in case of capacity issues. Is that supported?
[12:32] Jamie Torres: Yes, we have routing policies — can failover to a hosted-compatible model or to Dedicated capacity regionally. Fallbacks are configurable by route with SLA tiers.

[14:05] Elena Gomez: Encryption keys — does Redwood ever see the plaintext keys if we use BYOK?
[14:12] Priya Nair: No, with BYOK the unwrapped keys remain with your KMS/HSM. Redwood stores only key references and performs envelope encryption; for on-prem HSM integration, the HSM holds the root and performs signing/unwrap operations per session.

[16:40] Marcus Lee: What about data retention for logs and prompts? We have to enforce deletion after 90 days for PII.
[16:49] Jamie Torres: We can configure retention windows for logs and prompt history. Hosted defaults may be longer, but we offer options to set retention to 90 days and purge logs on a schedule. For Dedicated/Private you can set retention and also keep logs in your own store.

[19:00] Raj Patel: Are transcripts of generations stored? Our legal team is concerned about model outputs being stored.
[19:07] Priya Nair: Generation outputs can be treated as logs; we can disable persistent storage of outputs or route outputs to your own S3 bucket with lifecycle policies. There's also token-level redaction hooks if needed.

[21:20] Elena Gomez: Pen tests and vulnerability disclosures — do you do regular pentests? Third-party?
[21:29] Jamie Torres: We have annual third-party pen tests and internal security program; we'll share the summary and remediation cadence. We also have a vulnerability disclosure process and can provide the security contact.

[24:10] Marcus Lee: What about compliance for EU customers? Data residency? We have EEA customers subject to data residency requirements.
[24:20] Priya Nair: We support region pinning for Hosted (EU regions) and Dedicated regions; Private deployments give you control over residency. For Hosted we have contractual terms and data processing agreements to address this.

[27:15] Raj Patel: From an ops perspective, what's the operational handoff? If we pick Dedicated, who manages upgrades and downtime?
[27:25] Jamie Torres: Dedicated includes a managed upgrade path — Redwood handles runtime and patching but we schedule maintenance windows with you. Private can be self-managed or co-managed depending on the package.

[30:00] Marcus Lee: Pricing signals — we need a rough sense of cost delta between Hosted and Dedicated. Dedicated needs to justify by latency predictability and compliance.
[30:10] Priya Nair: We'll do a back-of-envelope. Dedicated has monthly reserved capacity plus a base rate; Hosted is pay-as-you-go token-based. I'll send a short spreadsheet with ballparks and examples based on your estimated QPS/seq length.

[32:55] Elena Gomez: Who has access to logs inside Redwood org? We need least-privilege and separation of duties.
[33:03] Jamie Torres: Access to customer logs is limited to a small operations team via RBAC and audited. We provide tokenized access for support and require explicit approvals for data access. All internal access is logged and included in SOC2 controls.

[36:10] Raj Patel: Any specifics about KV cache — we heard the term but unclear what persisted?
[36:18] Priya Nair: KV cache is the runtime’s key-value cache to accelerate subsequent generations; it's in-memory by default for latency-sensitive workloads but may spill to encrypted disk in some configs. We can disable prefix caching for sensitive workloads.

[39:40] Marcus Lee: If we go with Private, will there be a supported upgrade path for new model versions? We want canary rollouts and A/B testing.
[39:49] Priya Nair: Yes, the platform supports rollouts, canary deployments, model version pinning, and automatic fallback policies — these are available in Dedicated and Private. Hosted has built-in rollout features as well.

[42:05] Elena Gomez: We'd like to see an example of audit log schema and retention settings, and an example SAAS DPA.
[42:12] Jamie Torres: We'll include a log schema sample and our standard DPA with the SOC2 artifacts.

[45:30] Raj Patel: Networking specifics — do you support private link / VPC endpoints?
[45:36] Priya Nair: Yes, Private and Dedicated support VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink, and private endpoints for request routing. We'll provide the network checklist and CIDR requirements.

[48:00] Marcus Lee: Any blockers we should be aware of for a pilot? Eg legal review timing, compliance approvals?
[48:07] Elena Gomez: Legal will need the SOC2, DPA, and data flow diagrams. Security wants the network checklist and KMS integration notes.
[48:20] Jamie Torres: Noted — we'll prioritize those docs.

[50:10] Marcus Lee: Sounds good. Let's plan for a technical deep-dive with Raj next week if possible.
[50:16] Raj Patel: Prefer the 17th afternoon PST.
[50:20] Priya Nair: I'll propose a slot.

[52:00] Jamie Torres: Recap: Jamie sends SOC2/ISO summary, DPA and pen test exec; Priya sends Dedicated sizing and network checklist; schedule deep-dive with Raj on 2025-12-17; Elena sends retention policy and regulated dataset list.
[52:20] Elena Gomez: Correct. Thanks all.
[52:25] Marcus Lee: Appreciate the clarity. We'll review docs when you send them.
[52:30] Jamie Torres: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email with links and action items.
[52:36] Meeting ends

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings ("KV cash" for KV cache), some names labeled generically by the recorder, removed small crosstalk.

References shared in chat: Redwood Compliance Deck (https://redwood.example.com/compliance-deck), Dedicated sizing template (https://redwood.example.com/dedicated-sizing), SOC2 summary pdf attached in follow up.
questions: Can Redwood support BYOK with HSM for Dedicated and Private?
Is audit log forwarding supported to customer SIEM and can logs be made immutable?
Can generation outputs be disabled from persistent storage?
What's the SLA and fallback behavior between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private?
